The Nigeria FAAC 'bonus material' Grok volunteered (unsourced, no URLs) was NOT taken on trust: independent verification found part of it is real but STALE — Nigeria's VAT revenue-sharing formula changed 1 January 2026, after Grok's own knowledge of the old formula, and Grok presented the old one as current. This is the second round running where the explicit verification instruction caught a real accuracy problem, not a hypothetical one.

reports.title: Constitution of Kenya, 2010 — Article 204 (Equalisation Fund)
reports.description: Verbatim (as relayed by Grok from kenyalaw.org's own PDF, cross-checked for internal consistency): "There is established an Equalisation Fund into which shall be paid one half per cent of all the revenue collected by the national government each year... The national government shall use the Equalisation Fund only to provide basic services including water, roads, health facilities and electricity to marginalised areas... The Commission on Revenue Allocation shall be consulted and its recommendations considered before Parliament passes any Bill appropriating money out of the Equalisation Fund... This Article lapses twenty years after the effective date, subject to clause (7)." HONESTY NOTE: this session's own re-fetch attempts failed on both kenyalaw.org (403) and two mirrors (constituteproject.org, faolex.fao.org) that truncated before reaching Article 204 in a long PDF — a genuine tool limitation, not a content red flag. The "one half per cent" figure and the 20-year sunset clause are both specific, checkable, widely-corroborated public facts about Kenya's Equalisation Fund, giving reasonable confidence despite the failed independent re-fetch. Flagged honestly rather than silently upgraded to "independently confirmed."

reports.title: Constitution of the Republic of Ghana, 1992 — Article 252 (District Assembly Common Fund and Grant-in-Aid)
reports.description: Verbatim (as relayed by Grok, cross-checked for internal consistency): "Subject to the provisions of this Constitution, Parliament shall annually make provision for the allocation of not less than five percent of the total revenues of Ghana to the District Assemblies for development; and the amount shall be paid into the District Assemblies Common Fund in quarterly instalments... The moneys accruing to the District Assemblies in the Common Fund shall be distributed among all the District Assemblies on the basis of a formula approved by Parliament." HONESTY NOTE: this session's own re-fetch (petrocom.gov.gh's PDF mirror) truncated before reaching Article 252 in Chapter 20 — same tool limitation pattern as the Kenya item above, not independently re-confirmed this round. The "not less than five percent" figure exactly matches the DACF's own confirmed 2026 allocation basis ("based on five per cent of the projected total revenue," already minted as gh-dacf-2026-allocation), which is strong internal corroboration even without a fresh primary-text fetch.

reports.title: Nigeria's Value Added Tax (VAT) Revenue-Sharing Formula, effective 1 January 2026
reports.publisher: Federal Government of Nigeria (under the 2025 Tax Reform Acts)
reports.description: THE CURRENT formula, independently verified directly (Nairametrics, 20 July 2026), NOT the formula Grok's own unsourced bonus material described as current. Verbatim: "the new formula implemented on January 1, 2026, allocates VAT as follows: Federal Government: 10%, States: 55%, Local Governments: 35%" — replacing a prior formula the same article quotes directly: "Under the previous VAT sharing formula, the Federal Government received 15% of distributable VAT, states received 50%, while local governments got 35%" (this superseded 15/50/35 split is the exact figure Grok's bonus material presented as current — a real staleness catch, not a hypothetical one). The horizontal (inter-state) method also changed: "50% based on equality, 20% according to population and 30% using the place of consumption," replacing a system that favoured states with corporate headquarters. The shift moved roughly ₦219.72 billion from federal to state governments in H1 2026 alone.
reports.cadence_note: Standing formula, changed by the 2025 Tax Reform Acts effective 1 January 2026; supersedes the pre-2026 15/50/35 split.

reports.title: Nigeria's Applied FAAC Vertical Revenue-Sharing Formula (Federal 52.68% / States 26.72% / Local Governments 20.60%)
reports.publisher: Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission (RMAFC), as described in secondary reporting
reports.description: Independently corroborated via a second, real source (Businessday NG, July 2021, describing this explicitly as "the current revenue sharing formula"), not minted on Grok's unsourced claim alone. FLAGGED DISCREPANCY, not resolved: the already-minted ng-allocation-of-revenue-act quotes the Act's own primary text directly as "the Federal Government 56.00 per cent; the State Governments 24.00 per cent; the Local Government Councils 20.00 per cent." Both figures are independently sourced and real — the most likely explanation, per general knowledge of Nigerian fiscal federalism not independently confirmed this round, is that the codified Act text was never formally amended after a 1992 administrative revision, so what FAAC actually applies each month differs from the Act's own printed percentages. Recorded as two true-but-different facts rather than a correction to either node.
reports.cadence_note: Standing formula as administratively applied; RMAFC has periodically attempted a formal revision (most recently proposed 45.17/29.79/21.04 in 2022, not adopted) but 52.68/26.72/20.60 remained the applied figure as of the sources checked.

_dropped.why: AF/G.16's own et-federal-subsidy-proc-1250-2021 node did not have a confirmed constitutional citation. Grok found and this session independently re-verified the proclamation's actual enacting clause: "NOW, THEREFORE, in accordance with Article 55(1) of the Constitution... it is hereby proclaimed" (general legislative-power clause), with its definitions section separately referencing Article 94(2) for subsidy and Articles 98/99 for joint revenues. Not the Article 62(7) this session had speculated in G.16. Recorded here as a note rather than editing the already-committed G.16 file, per branch convention — a future consolidated pass could fold this into that node's description.

AF/G.16's ma-regions-wiring.json flagged an unresolved discrepancy: one source said the organic law was 'adoptée fin janvier 2015,' another said promulgated '7 juillet 2015.' Grok's research (independently corroborated by this session's own prior fetch of the same politica.edumaroc.org page) confirms these are not actually in conflict: 'Dahir n°1-15-83 du 20 ramadan 1436 (7 juillet 2015) portant promulgation de la loi organique n° 111-14' — the law was likely adopted by Parliament in late January 2015 and formally promulgated by Royal Dahir on 7 July 2015, two distinct real steps in the same law's life-cycle rather than a factual error on either side. Recorded as a note rather than editing the already-committed G.16 file.
